pkg.lyricsBlock:
[Verse 1]
I’m tired from loving you,
But I was scared those words would hurt you too
So I swallowed everything I wanted to say,
And only now I let them out
The me who wanted you all day long
Feels so far away now
Even when I call your name
My heart doesn’t answer anymore

[Pre-Chorus]
I want to walk away
But my feet won’t move
It’s not love that holds me here
It’s the guilt I can’t escape

[Chorus]
I want to breathe again
So I’ll let you go
Our love was just too big
“I’m sorry… I loved you”
Let me say it just once, for the last time
Now, for your sake,
I’ll let myself go

[Verse 2]
You still don’t know
How much I’ve been hurting inside
All those days I smiled and said “I’m okay”
They were never a lie

[Bridge]
That leaving first
Is the only thing I can give you
The last bit of kindness I have
I told myself that at least twenty-four times
Like a letter written in tears
I’m finally ending it

[Final Chorus]
I’m sorry… I want to live too
So I’m letting go of your hand
Because love is what made it hurt
Now I’ll set you free
Thank you… and I’m sorry
Not for you, but for me
I’ll quietly close the door
I love you…

[Outro]
I’m sorry…
I’m leaving now
pkg.sunoStyle:
Trendy pop with a soft, energetic groove. Modern, fresh and emotional.
Male-female duet vocals throughout. Alternating lines, natural vocal interplay, gentle harmonies, clear and expressive vocals. Keep both voices distinct and balanced.
Light and simple intro with soft harmony. Verses begin gently with light rhythm, subtle percussion and restrained bass. Pre-chorus gradually builds emotional tension through delicate textures and rhythmic movement, without sudden intensity.
Chorus adds warmth and energy with warm bass, gentle harmonies and a smooth rhythmic lift. Emotional and engaging, but controlled and never explosive.
Final section gradually reduces energy, returning to soft duet vocals and minimal accompaniment, ending calm and reflective.
Natural dynamics, warm tone, clean modern production. Avoid loud mastering, heavy bass, excessive drums, dense layers and aggressive instrumentation.
